messages:
harper: CI linkcheck on the mdx-migration branch flagged a weird set of anchors: some are missing, others resolve to the wrong subheading. blocking a few small user-facing docs fixes.

ci-bot: build: docs/mkdocs: linkcheck failed (exit 2). 13 broken fragment links. full log: https://ci.redwood/example/8233 :warning:

niko: examples: 
```
WARNING: broken link: ../guides/upgrade#v2-migration -> 404
WARNING: broken link: ../examples/usage#python-client-setup -> 404
WARNING: broken link: ../guides/perf#autoscale-ops -> 404
```

tara: pattern looks like three things: 1) headings with numbered prefixes ("1. Setup") lost the number in new slugs, 2) codefence-adjacent headings sometimes drop the slug, 3) emoji and non-ascii collapsed differently.

harper: ugh number prefixes. lots of internal references use anchors like `#1-setup` which now become `#setup` after slug change — explains the 404s. also saw duplicates where both "Setup" and "1. Setup" normalized inconsistently.

niko: short-term: surgical explicit ids for the pages reported by CI. i can open a small PR that only touches those files and adds `{#...}` ids with ascii kebab-case.

tara: agreed. prefer ids that match existing external links when possible (e.g. keep `1-setup` if external customers link to it). add a redirects map for any external legacy anchors we can't change.

harper: can we auto-detect which files to touch? i'd rather not mass-edit all headings.

links-bot: suggestion: run `scripts/anchor_mapper.py` against the CI log. it outputs candidate files and recommended `{#id}` to add. i can attach results to the PR as a checklist.

niko: nice. i'll generate the mapping and include it in the PR description so reviewers see the before/after. will also include local repro steps: 
```
pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
mkdocs build && mkdocs linkcheck --fail-on-broken
# or use the CI container to match env
docker run --rm -v $PWD:/src docs-ci:latest sh -c "cd /src && mkdocs linkcheck"
```

tara: small policy question: do we prefer adding `{#1-setup}` to preserve old external links or normalize to `{#setup}` and add redirects? i'd vote for preserving external links when obvious.

harper: preserve where we know external links exist; otherwise normalize and add redirect map entries for common legacy forms. let's keep PRs small and reversible.

niko: PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4610  touches 9 files, adds explicit ids, adds `scripts/anchor_mapper.py`, and a short CONTRIBUTING blurb recommending explicit ids for numbered headings, code-adjacent headings, and emoji.

ci-bot: note: linkcheck will re-run after PR updates. :info:

tara: i ran the mapper locally — it found 11 candidate anchors and suggested ids. i'm reviewing the PR now. small nit: change `1-setup` id to `step-1-setup` to avoid leading-number corner cases with some link parsers.

niko: updated PR per suggestion. also added a quick smoke test script `ci/smoke_anchors.sh` that curls a curated list of known anchors from staging after deploy. helps catch regressions post-merge.

harper: can we add a one-off CI job to post linkcheck failures as a PR comment with suggested ids? reduces manual triage. file an issue if you want to keep this PR focused.

links-bot: filed https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/246 recommending CI annotation of anchor failures and a bot that suggests exact `{#...}` fixes.

ci-bot: re-run queued for PR 4610...

tara: local mkdocs linkcheck passes for the edited files. left a couple small wording nits in the CONTRIBUTING addition.

niko: fixed and pushed. hoping for a quick merge if CI is green.

harper: thanks all  merging on green. after merge i'll kick off a full site rebuild and run the smoke anchors against staging, then report back here with final status. :rocket:

(last) ci-bot: PR 4610 linkcheck passed; ready to merge. :white_check_mark:
